## Measurement result: NO — id-string references cannot express these 16 defs today (evidence for objectstack#11592, not a workaround)

Tree measured: `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` @ `8c4073729ffe4b72cc4ab4422d5570ee47b9fbe7` (shallow clone, 1 commit visible, `2026-08-31T17:18:05Z`).

### Grep instrument controls

- Positive control: `grep -rln "record_header" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.json .` returns 7 files, all with real hits (see file list below) — the instrument finds a known-present string.
- Zero-hit probe: the same grep against `src/pages/*.page.ts` (the 4 record pages themselves) returns **zero** hits for the literal string `record_header`. Probed with a neighbouring known term — `grep -c "page:header"` on the same files returns non-zero for all 4 (`account_detail.page.ts:4`, `case_detail.page.ts:2`, `lead_detail.page.ts:2`, `opportunity_detail.page.ts:2`) — so the zero is real, not an instrument failure: the pages never spell the string `'record_header'` themselves because they don't inline a *new* ActionDef literal, they import the already-defined action **object** by identifier and place it directly in the `actions:` array.

### File list (`record_header` hits)

```
./src/actions/campaign.actions.ts
./src/actions/case.actions.ts
./src/actions/contact.actions.ts
./src/actions/global.actions.ts
./src/actions/knowledge_article.actions.ts
./src/actions/lead.actions.ts
./src/actions/opportunity.actions.ts
./test/metadata-references.test.ts
```

The 4 record pages carrying the 16 header-slot ActionDefs (confirmed by `test/metadata-references.test.ts`'s own `KNOWN_UNCONFORMING` set, which independently names the same 4 `*_header :: actions[]` locations):

```
./src/pages/account_detail.page.ts   (account_header_slotted)
./src/pages/case_detail.page.ts      (case_header)
./src/pages/lead_detail.page.ts      (lead_header)
./src/pages/opportunity_detail.page.ts (opp_header)
```

### The 16 defs — count matches the card exactly (3+3+5+5=16)

Every one of these is imported by identifier from `src/actions/*.actions.ts`, and every one of those same identifiers is also re-exported through `src/actions/index.ts` and spread into the app's registered-action stack in `objectstack.config.ts:178` (`actions: Object.values(actions)`). **This means the "inline" object and the "object-level registered action" are not two copies to diff — they are the same JS object in memory**, imported once and placed in both the header array and the app registry. `global.actions.ts`'s own docblock (line ~524) says this explicitly: "a page that imports `LogCallAction` and the stack that registers `ActivityActions` hold the SAME object."

| Page | Component id | Action id (`name`) | objectName | `locations` includes `record_header`? | Differs from registered action? | Expressible as `id` string reference? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| account_detail | account_header_slotted | `log_call` | crm_account | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| account_detail | account_header_slotted | `log_meeting` | crm_account | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| account_detail | account_header_slotted | `schedule_meeting` | crm_account | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| case_detail | case_header | `escalate_case` | crm_case | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| case_detail | case_header | `close_case` | crm_case | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| case_detail | case_header | `log_call` | crm_case | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| lead_detail | lead_header | `convert_lead` | crm_lead | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| lead_detail | lead_header | `schedule_followup` | crm_lead | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| lead_detail | lead_header | `log_call` | crm_lead | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| lead_detail | lead_header | `log_meeting` | crm_lead | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| lead_detail | lead_header | `schedule_meeting` | crm_lead | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| opportunity_detail | opp_header | `generate_quote` | crm_opportunity | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| opportunity_detail | opp_header | `clone_opportunity` | crm_opportunity | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| opportunity_detail | opp_header | `log_call` | crm_opportunity | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| opportunity_detail | opp_header | `log_meeting` | crm_opportunity | yes | no — same object | **NO** |
| opportunity_detail | opp_header | `schedule_meeting` | crm_opportunity | yes | no — same object | **NO** |

At the property level (`label`/`variant`/`icon`/`order`/`visible`/`requiredPermissions`/handler) there is **zero divergence** for any of the 16 — structurally guaranteed, since inline and registered are the same reference, not a copy. If the equivalence question were only "does the page override any field of the registered action," the answer would be a clean yes-all-16-equivalent.

**That is not the blocking finding.** The actual blocker is one level up, and it is dated, filed, and already sitting in this codebase's own test suite — `test/metadata-references.test.ts` lines ~408–459, `KNOWN_UNCONFORMING`, filed upstream as **hotcrm#1279**:

> `PageHeaderProps.actions` is `z.array(z.string())` ("Action IDs"), but objectui's canonical `page:header` renderer consumes ActionDef **objects**: it filters the array through `actionRendersAt(a, 'record_header')`, and reads `a.requiredPermissions` / `a.visible` / `a.name` / `a.order` **directly off each array element**. A string has no `.locations` (or `.requiredPermissions`/`.visible`/`.order`), so rewriting these four arrays as id strings "would turn this guard green and delete every header button from four record pages" — the same 4 pages and the same 16 defs this card asks about.

In other words: **there is no id → registered-action resolution step in objectui's `page:header` renderer today.** `actionRendersAt` and the property reads it needs are evaluated against the array element itself. Swap the object for a bare `'convert_lead'` string and `.locations` is `undefined` on every element — `actionRendersAt` has nothing to filter on, and per the filed evidence, **all 16 header action buttons across all 4 record pages disappear**. This is not a per-property customization gap (there is none) — it is a missing mechanism. `objectui#6252`'s "reference by id" plan needs that resolution step to exist in the renderer before hotcrm's headers could safely author id strings instead of objects; today, doing so is a straightforward regression, independent of any label/icon/order tuning.

### Positive control — one def, verbatim (`EscalateCaseAction`, `src/actions/case.actions.ts:13-25`)

```ts
export const EscalateCaseAction: Action = {
  name: 'escalate_case',
  label: 'Escalate Case',
  objectName: 'crm_case',
  icon: 'alert-triangle',
  type: 'flow',
  target: 'escalate_case',
  locations: ['record_header', 'list_item'],
  visible: P`record.is_escalated == false && record.is_closed == false`,
  confirmText: 'This will escalate the case to the escalation team. Continue?',
  successMessage: 'Case escalated successfully!',
  refreshAfter: true,
};
```

### Overall answer

**NO.** Per the card's own gate wording: this is evidence that **REOPENS the objectstack#11592 ruling** — it must not be worked around with an override semantic. Specifically: none of the 16 inline `record_header` ActionDefs across hotcrm's 4 record pages (`account_detail_page`, `case_detail_page`, `lead_detail_page`, `opportunity_detail_page`) is expressible today as a bare `id` string reference, because objectui's `page:header` renderer resolves `record_header` visibility and ordering (`actionRendersAt`, `.requiredPermissions`, `.visible`, `.order`) by reading those properties **directly off the array element**, and has no id → registered-action lookup. Converting any of the 4 pages' `actions:` arrays from objects to id strings is independently confirmed, in hotcrm's own dated test-suite commentary (filed as hotcrm#1279, `test/metadata-references.test.ts` `KNOWN_UNCONFORMING`), to delete every header action button on that page. This is not a property-divergence problem (the 16 defs are literally identical to their registered counterparts, being the same object); it is that the id-reference mechanism itself does not exist in the current renderer.

## Collection verdict (dispatching seat): measurement **ACCEPTED**, verdict mapping **CORRECTED** — the gate PASSES; nothing reopens objectstack#11592

The reading above (comment 5486736502, hotcrm @ `8c40737`) is exactly what the card asked for and the controls are sound. But its overall "NO — reopens the ruling" maps the measurement onto the wrong question, and the correction changes the routing:

- **The card's gate** (objectui#6252 Step 1): *does any inline def carry page-level customization an id-resolved action cannot express?* The measurement answers: **all 16 inline defs are the same JS object as their object-level registered actions — zero divergence, zero page-level customization.** That is the strongest possible PASS of the equivalence gate.
- **What the dev's "NO" actually observed**: today's `page:header` renderer reads properties off array elements with no id→registered-action resolution step, so swapping objects for id strings *before the fix lands* deletes the buttons. That fact is **objectstack#11592's own premise** (its body: "a string has no `.locations`, so every entry is filtered out") — the defect the ruling rules on, not new evidence against it. objectui#6252 is precisely the card that builds the resolution step; its content already covers the transition ("keep the existing object-shape handling working during the transition if it is cheap; the contract of record is ids").

⇒ **Routing**: objectui#6252 is UNBLOCKED to implement (label flipped in the same pass); nothing goes back to objectstack#11592. The hotcrm migration to id references stays downstream of #6252's landing, exactly as that card records.

This card's ask is fully answered — closing `completed`. The measurement's per-def table remains the reference for #6252's implementer.
